articleTitle: Google Will Disable AI in Schools Unless Search Is Also Turned Off

sources.title: Google will let schools disable its AI tools, but not without sacrificing Search - TechCrunch

Google will let schools skip AI tools, but they have to give up search, too

claims.claim: Google announced on Tuesday that it plans to disable AI tools for K‑12 students next year unless school administrators explicitly turn them on, revising its approach across Gemini, NotebookLM, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search, according to a statement by Chris Phillips, vice president for education at Google.
claims.bestSource: Google will let schools disable its AI tools, but not without sacrificing Search - TechCrunch
claims.evidence: Google announced on Tuesday that it plans to disable AI tools for K-12 students next year unless school administrators explicitly turn them on. The tech giant says the change follows consultations with schools, teachers, leading researchers, and policymakers. As a result, Google is revising its approach across Gemini, NotebookLM, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search. Chris Phillips, vice president for education at Google, told The New York Times that “Search and AI are deeply integrated,” which means that if a school chooses to restrict AI altogether, students “will not have access to search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available.” However, Google Search and its AI features are now inseparable. Given the dominance of Google’s suite of apps in classrooms and the widespread use of Chromebooks, the decision underscores the company’s influence over the education sector. Google announced the upcoming change alongside the launch of Guided Learning in schools. The tool, which was unveiled earlier this year, sort of functions like an AI tutor, as it’s designed to help users build a deep understanding instead of just getting answers. The launch comes amid concerns that AI chatbots undermine the learning process because they spit out direct answers. Although teachers may not want students to use AI Overviews in Google Search to conduct research or complete assignments, they likely still want them to be able to have access to the search engine to find sources and other learning materials.
